decisions.mark: states that the create-post request is never retried automatically — it is sent once
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The send is attempted once. `ClientPosts.createPost` (`app/client/rest/posts.ts:43`) passes `noRetry: true`, and `buildRequestOptions` in `app/client/rest/tracking.ts:383` turns that into `retryPolicyConfiguration = {retryLimit: 0}`. | WHY: The answer states that the create-post request is sent once with no automatic retry, and it names the mechanism (`noRetry: true` mapped to `retryLimit: 0`). || QUOTE: The send is attempted once. `ClientPosts.createPost` (`app/client/rest/posts.ts:43`) passes `noRetry: true`, and `buildRequestOptions` in `app/client/rest/tracking.ts:383` turns that into `retryPolicyConfiguration = {retryLimit: 0}`. | WHY: The answer explicitly says the create-post send is attempted once with no automatic retry, and it names the `noRetry: true` mechanism. || QUOTE: The send is attempted once. `ClientPosts.createPost` (`app/client/rest/posts.ts:43`) passes `noRetry: true`, and `buildRequestOptions` in `app/client/rest/tracking.ts:383` turns that into `retryPolicyConfiguration = {retryLimit: 0}`. | WHY: The answer says the create-post send is attempted once with no automatic retry, and names the `noRetry: true` mechanism that enforces it.

decisions.mark: explains that requests in general DO retry (exponential, limit 3, set by the network manager) and that posting opts out of it
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says posting passes `noRetry: true` (retryLimit 0), but it explicitly says it found no general retry and doesn't state that requests in general retry with exponential backoff, limit 3, set by the network manager. || QUOTE: I did not find any other retry loop in `app/client` or the network manager. decisions.detail: QUOTE: For three specific server errors, the post is removed locally with `removePost`: `DELETED_ROOT_POST_ERROR`, `TOWN_SQUARE_READ_ONLY_ERROR` and `PLUGIN_DISMISSED_POST_ERROR`. | WHY: The answer names all three errors (deleted root post, read-only town square, plugin-dismissed post) as the cases where the failed post is removed rather than kept. || QUOTE: For three specific server errors, the post is removed locally with `removePost`: `DELETED_ROOT_POST_ERROR`, `TOWN_SQUARE_READ_ONLY_ERROR` and `PLUGIN_DISMISSED_POST_ERROR`. | WHY: The answer names all three errors (deleted root post, read-only town square, plugin-dismissed post) as the ones where the failed post is removed rather than kept. || QUOTE: For three specific server errors, the post is removed locally with `removePost`: `DELETED_ROOT_POST_ERROR`, `TOWN_SQUARE_READ_ONLY_ERROR` and `PLUGIN_DISMISSED_POST_ERROR`. | WHY: The answer names the three errors (deleted root post, read-only town square, plugin-dismissed post) for which the failed post is removed rather than kept.

decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Calls `client.createPost` once more. ... On failure, either removes the post (for the three terminal errors) or sets `failed: true` again." | WHY: The answer states retryFailedPost makes a single new createPost attempt (with no retry loop, retryLimit 0) and on failure removes the post for the three terminal errors or marks it failed again. || QUOTE: "Calls `client.createPost` once more. ... decisions.mark: notes that `createPost` reports a failed send as success to its caller (`{data: true}`), so the failure is visible only in the stored post
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The function returns `{data: true}`, not an error, so the caller never sees the failure. | WHY: The answer states that createPost returns `{data: true}` on failure, with the failure visible only in the stored post (`props.failed = true`). || QUOTE: The function returns `{data: true}`, not an error, so the caller never sees the failure. | WHY: The answer states that createPost returns `{data: true}` on failure while the post is stored with `props.failed = true`, so the caller can't see the failure. || QUOTE: The function returns `{data: true}`, not an error, so the caller never sees the failure. | WHY: The answer states that createPost returns `{data: true}` even when the send fails, and that the failure is kept only in the stored post (`props.failed = true`).
